paper.title_en: Beyond de Sitter: Longitudinal-Mode Instabilities and Spectral Evolution of Massive Vector Fields with Non-Minimal Curvature Coupling during Inflation
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the inflationary dynamics and spectral energy densities of a massive spectator vector field non-minimally coupled to the Ricci scalar. We compare exact de Sitter (dS) and constant-slow-roll quasi-de Sitter (qdS) backgrounds, following transverse and longitudinal modes through an instantaneous transition to radiation domination. We initialize the modes deep inside the horizon with second-order WKB Bunch--Davies conditions and solve their equations numerically for representative comoving momenta and vector masses. The non-minimal coupling modifies the effective mass, canonical normalization, and effective-mass-crossing time, while leaving the horizon-crossing condition fixed by the prescribed background in the spectator-field approximation. At mass crossing, the transverse spectral energy density increases slightly and monotonically over 0 <= xi <= 10^{-6}, whereas the longitudinal density decreases monotonically, with an approximately 21% suppression from xi = 0 to 10^{-6} in both backgrounds. The qdS longitudinal values remain slightly above their dS counterparts, while the transverse results are nearly indistinguishable. Despite its suppression, the longitudinal contribution remains dominant, exceeding the transverse contribution by approximately three orders of magnitude. We also derive an all-momentum condition for a non-negative longitudinal canonical frequency in exact de Sitter space. For the representative mass considered, the required coupling lies outside the constant-coefficient heavy-scalar matching regime, so large-coupling solutions are formal rather than controlled effective-theory predictions. Our results distinguish kinetic positivity, canonical-frequency signs, bare spectral energy densities, and the validity domain of the effective description.
